source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Clean the stump routinely with rubbing alcohol after diaper changes and keep it covered with dry gauze until separation.","B":"Keep it clean and dry, fold the diaper below it, and use sponge baths until it falls off.","C":"Apply petroleum jelly routinely so the stump remains moist until separation.","D":"Begin routine tub baths while the stump is attached as long as it is dried afterward."}}
source_row.rationale: AAP guidance recommends dry cord care: keep the stump clean and dry, fold the diaper below it to promote air exposure, and use sponge baths until the cord separates. Option B therefore best reflects routine home care. Option A adds routine alcohol and gauze that are not recommended for an uncomplicated stump. Option C keeps the stump moist and covered, contrary to dry-cord care. Option D introduces tub bathing while the stump remains attached rather than using sponge baths.
source_row.source_detail: American Academy of Pediatrics HealthyChildren.org — Umbilical Cord Symptoms/Care: keep stump clean/dry, fold diaper below for air contact, use sponge baths until cord falls off; avoid routine rubbing alcohol.
